sampling_model.design: A fixed finite population is partitioned into \(m\) labeled clusters; the chosen law \(D\) randomizes jointly over cluster saturation labels and exact treated subsets.
sampling_model.units: Potential outcomes \(Y_{g i}(z,a)\) are fixed; there is no superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: Cluster \(g\) receives label \(A_g\), then exactly \(r_{s_g,A_g}\) of its \(s_g\) units are treated.
sampling_model.overlap: The general endpoint, orbit-game, frontier, and compiler results allow every feasible count \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant menus. A local condition \(1\le r_{q,a}<q\) is used only to produce the higher-order observation obstruction for that realized cluster-label cell. The strict-separation and complement-symmetry specializations directly fix \(r_{3,1}=1\) and \(r_{3,2}=2\); their proofs check \(0<r_{3,a}<3\) and \(r_{3,1}\ne r_{3,2}\) from those displayed numbers and use no global interiority or saturation-variation assumption. Optimal designs may assign zero probability to labels or assignment orbits.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the estimator is chosen jointly with the randomization and may be nonlinear in the revealed outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 derives standard errors and power criteria for individual saturation and slope effects under a clustered regression model.
Theorem 1 shows that independent fair assignment with a nonlinear estimator is minimax over bounded no-interference potential outcomes.
Theorem 2.3 Bernoulli-lifts the binary no-interference minimax experiment to bounded outcomes and decodes a nonlinear rule.
Proposition 2.2 expresses the arbitrary-neighborhood-interference minimax risk as a function of a pairwise conflict graph.
The paper optimizes bias and variance of the difference-in-means estimator across randomized saturation designs under a linear interference model.
Theorem 2.1 proves minimax complete randomization by group averaging under permutation invariance for a fixed invariant estimator.

body.tldr: Randomized saturation experiments reveal overlapping vectors of own-treatment-by-saturation responses, so their unrestricted design-and-estimation problem is neither a no-interference tensor product nor a pairwise conflict-graph game. Every realized interior cluster-label cell has a higher-order minimal nonface: with \(h\) equal to the larger treatment-arm size, all \(h\)-subsets of \(h+1\) same-arm coordinates are observable but the full set is not. For fixed saturation count and bounded cluster size, every feasible treated-count table, including boundary counts and a label-constant menu, reduces exactly to a rational endpoint orbit game over all correlated designs, bounded schedules, and measurable estimators. Conditional uniform subset randomization is without loss, and independent-saturation minimaxity has a finite complete positive-support saddle characterization: positive design orbits are dual best responses, positive prior orbits have primal risk equal to the value, and positive-likelihood cells use posterior means. The certified two-cluster instance has a strict correlated-saturation advantage on an infinite rational contrast neighborhood. The bit-certified compiler returns weak rational certificates and a total zero-face-safe decoder without claiming rational exact optimizers.

project_justification.gap: Saturation-design papers optimize power or the bias and variance of specified regression or inverse-probability estimators, while recent unrestricted minimax papers either assume no interference or replace observation feasibility by a pairwise conflict graph. Such a graph necessarily fills in the forbidden \(h+1\)-set created by any interior exact-count cell because all of its \(h\)-subsets, hence all pairs, are observable. Existing work also does not give the full positive-support saddle equalities for optimized common-probability independent saturation.
project_justification.niche: Fixed saturation-label count and bounded cluster size leave exponentially many labeled schedules but only polynomially many size-tagged response, assignment, and observation histograms, whether treated counts are interior, on the boundary, or constant across labels. That symmetry permits an exact decision-theoretic quotient without assuming independence or linearity.
project_justification.fill: The paper establishes endpoint completeness and a stabilizer-weighted rational primal-dual orbit game for every feasible count table, with implementable correlated randomization and nonlinear estimation. It proves the general local-interiority obstruction, retaining the size-three control triple as the minimal corollary, and gives a finite independent-design feasibility frontier with equality on every positive design and least-favorable-prior support point and posterior-mean decisions on every positive-likelihood cell. A strict rational separation certificate and the bit-certified compiler complete the design result; the compiler returns checkable rational \(\varepsilon\)-saddles and a total zero-face-safe decoder in polynomial time in the stated encoding measures.

body.related_work: BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018 provides the motivating fixed-count randomized-saturation design and its direct and spillover analysis, but not an unrestricted finite-population minimax estimator or a bit-certified joint design algorithm. AronowSamii2017 supplies exposure mappings, exposure-probability bookkeeping, and design-based estimation under general interference; the present paper instead optimizes jointly over every measurable estimator and every feasible correlated exact-count design. HudgensHalloran2008, BasseFeller2018, and JiangImaiMalani2023 develop the design-based two-stage causal framework without the present all-estimator finite saddle characterization. Bai2023 proves complete randomization by permutation-invariance group averaging for a fixed invariant estimator; here group averaging reduces the entire design--estimator--nature game and retains arbitrary correlated saturation actions. CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022 optimizes randomized and deterministic saturation designs for a specified difference-in-means estimator under linear interference, whereas the present criterion is worst-case finite-population squared error over all bounded schedules and all measurable estimators. Kallus2021 establishes mixed-strategy design optimality at a general decision-theoretic level, while the present result constructs and weakly optimizes the exact rational observation-hypergraph quotient. Sion1958 supplies the standard compact-minimax substrate used to equate the primal and dual values of the finite orbit game, rather than a new saturation-specific reduction. GrotschelLovaszSchrijver1988 supplies generic weak rational convex optimization; the novelty here is compiling the rational exact-count hypergraph orbit game, handling its zero-probability faces, and decoding its certified nonlinear estimator. The accepted-bank paper \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} supplies the finite unrestricted response-orbit minimax and rational-program certificate architecture in the no-interference setting. The present paper inherits that finite minimax architecture, but adds the exact-count higher-order observation hypergraph, the quotient of arbitrary correlated saturation-label actions, the stabilizer-weighted exact kernel, the conditional-uniformity reduction, and a total zero-face-safe decoder with a bit-certified compiler. Hull2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026 supply endpoint reductions in no-interference experiments, whereas the present compiler covers bounded anonymous saturation interference, arbitrary correlated first-stage laws, boundary treated counts, and label-constant menus. KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies a pairwise conflict-graph experiment; here every interior exact-count cell yields \(h+1\) same-arm coordinates whose \(h\)-subsets are all observable although the full set is not, so no pairwise graph represents the compatibility complex.
body.interpretation: For a fixed menu of saturation labels and bounded cluster sizes, an experimental team can compile the exact finite observation experiment rather than approximate it by pairwise conflicts. A single interior cluster-label cell already certifies when such a graph approximation is invalid. Rational weights specify how to randomize saturation histograms and treated subsets, the endpoint table specifies a possibly nonlinear analysis rule, and two directly checkable rational inequalities bracket the worst-case causal mean-squared error within any requested rational tolerance. The independent-design frontier additionally checks all positive supports on both sides of the saddle, while the continuous-outcome rule remains total on structurally impossible or prior-null observations.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The compiler guarantee is polynomial in the displayed orbit-program size for fixed \(K\) and \(b\); it does not make the constant-size response alphabet small in practice and is not a strongly polynomial algorithm. Exact rational arithmetic may produce large certificates even though their bit length is polynomial. The numerical size-three witness remains supported by its separate exhaustive rational verifier, while the compiler theorem supplies the general symbolic kernel construction, global oracle geometry, erosion-correct weak optimization, tolerance accounting, and decoder proof rather than a new numerical rerun. The strict separation is a finite-game, contrast-neighborhood result; no topology on observable laws or asymptotic experiment sequence is part of the theorem.
body.honest_scope: Endpoint completeness, the exact orbit game, and the bit-certified compiler cover every rational feasible table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant treated-count menus. Hypergraph nonrepresentability is local: it follows whenever a realized cluster-label cell has \(1\le r_{q,a}<q\), with no claim for a table consisting only of boundary cells. The independent-saturation result is a finite primal-dual feasibility and positive-support saddle characterization, not an elementary closed-form classification. The compiler returns rational weakly optimal certificates and a total continuous estimator; it does not claim exact rational optimizers or a separation as the number of clusters tends to infinity. The strict advantage is only the certified two-cluster exact-count game and its stated infinite rational contrast neighborhood. It does not claim robustness in an ambient observable-law topology, nondegenerate superpopulation conditional support or variance, positive region mass, or asymptotic persistence; those would be different strengthening projects, not premises of the stated finite minimax inequality.
